subject: POC observability & success criteria — Acme Corp trial
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: POC scope & observability needs

Hi Jordan / Alex,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the team. I wanted to capture the high-level POC goals so our engineering team can prioritize:

- Objective: Validate Redwood Inference for real-time recommendations in our checkout flow (50–200 token prompts, peak 120 qps).
- Success criteria (initial):
  * p95 end-to-end latency < 300ms on 20-token prompts under 75 qps sustained
  * Error rate (5xx + model failures) < 0.5%
  * Token cost per 1k requests within agreed budget range (TBD value)
  * No data exfiltration — logs retained in our S3 bucket only

We specifically need an observability plan for the POC: dashboards, tracing, which metrics you’ll expose, where logs will go, retention windows, and alerting thresholds. I attached our Acme_POC_requirements.xlsx with example traffic patterns and a short checklist of compliance items.

Next steps from our side: we can provide a VPN jump host and service account by next Tue (23 Feb). Would you share a proposed timeline and who on your side will own the monitoring setup?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Senior Product Manager — Acme Corp
samira.k@acme.com

-----Attachment: Acme_POC_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC scope & observability needs

Hi Samira — great to meet you too. Appreciate the clear goals and the spreadsheet. Below is our proposed POC observability & evaluation plan, ownership, and a compact timeline. I’m copying Alex (Solutions) and Laura (CS) for operational coverage.

High-level POC plan (2-week core trial + 1 onboarding window):
- Week 0 (onboard): networking + credentials, baseline slow tests, deploy Redwood test instance in your VPC (private deployment mode).
- Week 1 (baseline + steady-state): run representative traffic (you provided) at 30–75 qps, collect metrics and logs.
- Week 2 (stress + edge cases): scale to peak patterns, run cold-start/kv-cache eviction tests, and failover scenarios.
- Final day: joint review, pass/fail against agreed success criteria and handoff notes.

POC owners:
- Redwood account lead: Jordan Blake (me) — contract/coordination and acceptance
- Redwood solutions engineer: Alex Martinez — observability, dashboard build, tracing integration
- Redwood customer success: Laura Bennett — onboarding, runbooks, post-POC recommendations
- Acme owners: Samira Khan (PM), Ben Lee (Eng lead) — provide test traffic and env access

Observability deliverables we will provide (by end of Week 0):
- Grafana dashboards (proposed):
  * Overview: p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate (rps), error rate, token usage, token_cost_per_krequest
  * Model health: model_response_time_by_layer, kv_cache_hit_rate, kv_cache_size, gpu_utilization
  * Queueing/backpressure: request_queue_length, inference_worker_idle_pct, tokens_per_request
  * Cost telemetry: tokens_generated_per_min, estimated_cost_per_hour, average_tokens_per_request
- Tracing: Distributed traces (Jaeger compatible) capturing client->gateway->model runtime spans; span tags to include prompt_length, model_variant, customer_id
- Logs: Structured inference logs (JSON) exported to your S3 bucket + a streaming copy to our internal blob for ephemeral debugging (30-day retention). We can opt-out of sending copies on request.
- Alerts: out-of-the-box alerts we’ll configure in Grafana: p95 latency > 350ms (warning), > 450ms (critical); error_rate > 1% (critical); gpu_utilization > 95% for 2m (warning)

Metrics we plan to emit (examples):
- request.latency.p50, request.latency.p95, request.latency.p99
- request.rate (rps)
- request.error.count, request.error.rate
- tokens.generated.count, tokens.cost.estimated
- kv_cache.hit_rate, kv_cache.size_bytes
- model.infer.time_ms, model.queue.length
- infra.gpu.utilization_pct, infra.mem.usage_bytes

Data/retention/security notes:
- Logs to Acme S3 with lifecycle policy you control. Default retention: 90 days unless Acme requests 30/365.
- Audit logs for admin actions will be provided as CSV exports on request.
- We will provide a short SOC 2 evidence package for the POC scope before Week 0 if needed (Laura will coordinate).

Attachments: I’ve attached a Redwood_POC_observability_template.pdf that shows a sample dashboard layout and export schema.

Next actions / asks:
1) Samira / Ben: confirm the success criteria above (I copied your p95/ER items and filled in defaults where useful).
2) Provide service account + S3 write role and VPN details by Tue 23 Feb.
3) Alex will send a short checklist for telemetry endpoints we’ll instrument in your test harness.

I’ll create a draft Mutual Action Plan and share a Drive link by EOD.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

-----Attachment: Redwood_POC_observability_template.pdf (document stub)
From: Ben Lee <ben.lee@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC scope & observability needs

Thanks Jordan — this looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our eng side:

- Add 99th percentile latency target to the success criteria if possible (we’d like p99 < 600ms).
- Availability: we expect the service to be reachable 99% of the time during the POC window (synthetic checks from three regions).
- For logs, please confirm the retention options (30 / 90 / 365 days) and encryption-at-rest details — we need to be SOC2-compliant for the trial data.

If you can update the mutual action plan with those three items, we can sign and aim for onboarding the week of 23 Feb.

Cheers,
Ben Lee
Platform Engineering Lead — Acme Corp
ben.lee@acme.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Lee <ben.lee@acme.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@acme.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC scope & observability needs

Ben / Samira — thanks, noted and we’ll incorporate. Quick confirmations: 

- p99 target: we will include p99 < 600ms as an acceptance criterion (added to the MAP).
- Availability: we will set up synthetic probes (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and include uptime in the dashboard; target 99% during POC.
- Retention / encryption: logs to Acme S3 will be server-side encrypted (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS per your preference). Retention buckets we support: 30 / 90 / 365 days — default 90. We’ll add an option to expire earlier on request.

Operational note: Alex will provision a temporary Grafana org and pre-build the dashboard tiles (I’ve attached a static sample graphic). We’ll hand over the dashboard and alert runbook at the end of Week 0 so your team can validate metrics mapping.

Immediate next steps (I’ll action these today):
- Draft Mutual Action Plan (Drive link) and send for signature.
- Alex: send telemetry checklist + prometheus metric names to Ben.
- Laura: prepare SOC2 evidence subset for the POC and list of required docs.

We’ll plan the kickoff call for Mon 23 Feb 10:00 PT pending your access info. If that slot doesn’t work, tell me preferred times.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
